name: MO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Wesley Bell running with $3.6M raised
Polymarket prices Bell at 98% to win
model.rationale: The district's +29 Democratic lean, Bell's incumbency and strong fundraising, and prediction markets pricing him near certain victory all point the same direction, with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Bell would be the only plausible route to narrowing this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Wesley Bell, a first-term Democratic incumbent, defends a St. Louis-area seat whose partisan lean favors Democrats by roughly 29 points. He enters the general election after winning his primary with strong financial backing, having raised about $3.6 million and holding over $1 million on hand, plus modest outside support. His Republican opponent, Paul Berry, shows no reported fundraising, and a Libertarian is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price Bell's chances near 98 percent. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all aligned, the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
